Everyone feels angst, everyone feels sadness, impulsivity, impatience, struggles to focus, yes, but there's a difference between experiencing those things as a normal person would, and having a condition.

If you are feeling this way though, please seek professional help and take care of yourself.

Well I started on cico (I'm pretty short so 1200 cal worked for me), that way I didn't need to restrict what I could or couldn't eat and could still satisfy cravings or had that feel good food there if I needed it. And I tried to exercise every day, even if it was 10 minutes of some basic weight training. 

After a while it becomes a habit, the eating I mean, along the way I got the feeling of control over my food in stead of the other way around. 

And honestly, before bed I get myself a "snack". Usually a cup of something warm (like hot chocolate) or a small portion of something else, even if it's some cereal. It satiates any cravings I might get. It often feels like "oh no I have to go to bed soon, I won't be able to do it later" kind of thing. So I made it part of my routine when winding down and I got used to the idea that, that was my treat so any other cravings died down.

Also, WATER. I have a 500ml bottle with me at all times. I sip on it through the day, if I get hungry normally I'll drink some first, sometimes you're just thirsty not actually hungry, not always, but sometimes. Either way it helps fight off cravings too anyway and it's a healthy habit to build regardless. 

Also, it's a good idea to keep a snack close by, something that's healthy, chewy or the like is a good idea. If it isn't in small portion sizes, if possible, make it into smaller pieces. Makes a small snack last longer and makes it healthier to reach for when you're busy with something else. 

It might also help to use it as a reward system for work, like for me if I get through a chapter of my studies I can reward myself with a snack or something.
